stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria and null spec on a complex cross-team live preview feature requiring real-time content rendering, state synchronization, and iframe/security boundary considerations. Openspec needed first to elaborate requirements and define ACs; speckit then hardens testability, security, and edge cases (draft vs published state, partial content, error states).

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — Contentstack Live Preview does not exist in the codebase. The central attachment point is useContent (236 callers); all Contentstack components (ContentstackLink, ContentstackImage, ContentstackTable, etc.) consume it and should work unchanged once the hook supports live updates. VCs derived from description since ACs are empty. External service constraint applied: VCs stop at our boundary and assume Contentstack client is mocked where needed.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array, so all criteria above are new. They are derived solely from the story title, description, and the file paths listed in technicalNotes — file contents were NOT available for review. Key areas covered: (1) core live-preview behavior for text, image, link, and table content (AC-1 through AC-4), (2) transparent useContent hook integration for all 236 consumers (AC-5), (3) opt-in/non-preview safety (AC-6, AC-18, AC-19), (4) ContentstackContext lifecycle (AC-7, AC-8), (5) connection resilience — drop and reconnect (AC-9, AC-10), (6) performance under rapid edits (AC-11), (7) error handling — SDK init failure and malformed data (AC-12, AC-13), (8) SSR/hydration safety (AC-14), (9) accessibility — screen reader announcements and focus preservation (AC-15, AC-16), (10) security — no raw HTML injection from preview payloads (AC-17), (11) type safety for content interfaces (AC-20). If file contents had been available, criteria around specific data-shape handling in contentCard.ts or existing ContentstackContext patterns might have been refined further.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Openspec failed its primary mandate: it produced an empty acceptanceCriteria array despite being assigned to elaborate requirements and define ACs for a complex cross-team live-preview feature. Its contribution was limited to architectural observations (identifying useContent as the attachment point with 236 callers, noting existing components should work unchanged) — valuable context but not AC elaboration. Speckit then compensated by deriving 20 ACs from title/description/file paths alone, with file contents explicitly NOT available for review. While speckit's coverage is broad (core behavior, integration, opt-in safety, connection resilience, performance, error handling, SSR/hydration, accessibility, security, type safety), the entire AC set is inferred rather than grounded in actual code patterns. The pipeline did not function as designed: openspec should elaborate and speckit should harden/review — instead speckit did all the work from scratch on an empty input. Additionally, both agents report acceptanceChanged=false despite speckit stating all criteria are new, suggesting a possible data integrity issue in the pipeline output. Human review needed to (1) validate the 20 inferred ACs against actual codebase patterns in ContentstackContext and contentCard.ts, (2) confirm whether openspec's empty AC output was a pipeline failure or intentional handoff, and (3) reconcile the acceptanceChanged discrepancy.
